written:
## 1. The numbers
Cautious but not panicked. Stocks recovered from an early dip, but gold and bitcoin fell and the VIX edged higher. Rate-hike expectations and the Nvidia shock set the tone.

## 2. What moved and why
**Nvidia drops after CEO Jensen Huang resigns**
Why it happened: Nvidia said Huang resigned as CEO, president and board member effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO.
Why it matters: Nvidia sits at the center of the AI trade, so a leadership gap with no clear successor hit chip peers even as the broader indexes recovered.

**Gold slides as traders price a December Fed hike**
Why it happened: Markets now fully price in a December Fed rate hike after stronger US inflation and hawkish Fed remarks. The dollar also hit a 19-month high.
Why it matters: Higher rates and a firmer dollar reduce the appeal of an asset that pays no interest.

**Bitcoin falls to its lowest since August**
Why it happened: Nvidia's CEO news and MSCI's confirmation that Strategy will leave its indexes pushed bitcoin below $72,000.
Why it matters: Crypto is trading like a leveraged tech asset, and fund outflows are adding pressure.

## Deals
- **Acquisition: Marvell → Lumentum** (About $115 billion enterprise value, all stock). It pairs Marvell's electrical technology with Lumentum's optical expertise for AI data centers.
- **Acquisition: Shield AI → Echodyne** (Up to $5.3 billion). Shield buys the counter-drone radar maker and is raising $2.5 billion to fund it.
- **Financing: Public investors → KDP** ($2 billion underwritten share offering). KDP shares fell 5% after it launched the sale.

## Already out today
- Before the open: Nebius Q3 results. Revenue of $980.9M vs $907.5M expected. The shares still fell 19% because the 2026 revenue range came in slightly below estimates.

## 3. What's coming today
- Tonight (after close): Cisco and Applied Materials earnings. They give a read on AI networking and chip-equipment demand.
- Rest of the week: Fed officials speaking. Several Fed officials are set to speak.

## 4. Canada corner
- Gold producers, a big part of Canada's equity market, face a weaker price backdrop.
- I found no major Canadian deals in my searches.

## 5. The takeaway
Nvidia's leadership gap shows how concentrated the AI trade is: one CEO exit hit chip peers and dragged crypto, while rate-hike bets weighed on gold.

stories.title: Nvidia drops after CEO Jensen Huang resigns
stories.why_happened: Nvidia said Huang resigned as CEO, president and board member effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO.
stories.why_matters: Nvidia sits at the center of the AI trade, so a leadership gap with no clear successor hit chip peers even as the broader indexes recovered.
stories.full: Nvidia has been the core of this year's AI-driven rally. The news arrived a day after a chip-led rebound, when the Nasdaq jumped 1.60% and the S&P 500 gained 1.31%. Nvidia fell 14% at the open, then trimmed losses to roughly 7%. By late morning it was down about 5.6%. At least four brokers downgraded the stock, worried that an investigation could last five months or longer with no obvious succession plan. Indexes pared earlier losses and turned green. The reaction was uneven across chips. Intel and Micron fell, while rival AMD rose. Broadcom also advanced. Nvidia's web of tie-ups with other AI companies makes the wider fallout hard to size. The stock has dropped roughly 30% over the past month. Watch for a permanent CEO announcement, any detail on the investigation, and tonight's Cisco and Applied Materials results for AI demand signals.

stories.full: Gold had been hovering around $4,000. It slipped back below that level for the third time since late October. Tuesday's hotter US inflation report started the move, and a stronger dollar makes gold costlier for non-US buyers while higher Treasury yields make it less attractive. The selloff spread across metals. Silver lost 3.47% and copper slid 1.8%. North American gold ETFs lost $512 million in October, the only region with outflows, according to the World Gold Council. Holders of dollar and short-dated bonds benefit from higher yields. Gold producers, a big part of Canada's equity market, face a weaker price backdrop. Next up is Friday's producer price report. One strategist sees gold possibly falling toward $3,870, near its late-October low, if PPI beats forecasts.

intern.headline: Nvidia CEO exit rattles AI trade, gold slumps
intern.mood: Cautious but not panicked. Stocks bounced back from an early drop. Gold and bitcoin fell, and the VIX (a gauge of how nervous traders are) edged higher. Bets on higher interest rates and the Nvidia shock set the tone.

stories.title: Nvidia drops after CEO Jensen Huang resigns
stories.why_happened: Nvidia said Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and board member, effective immediately. CFO (chief financial officer, the person who runs the money side of a company) Colette Kress was named interim CEO (a temporary boss).
stories.why_matters: Nvidia is at the center of the AI trade (the wave of buying in companies that build or use artificial intelligence). With no clear new leader, chip companies nearby also got hit, even as the wider market recovered.
stories.full: Nvidia has been the heart of this year's AI-driven rally. The news arrived a day after a rebound led by chip stocks. The Nasdaq (a stock index full of tech companies) jumped 1.60%, and the S&P 500 (a index of 500 large US companies) gained 1.31%. Nvidia fell 14% when trading opened. Then it recovered some ground and dropped about 7%. By late morning it was down about 5.6%. At least four brokers (firms that advise people on buying and selling stocks) cut their rating on the stock. They worry an investigation could last five months or longer, and there is no clear plan for who leads next. The big indexes shrank their early losses and turned positive. The reaction was mixed across chip stocks. Intel and Micron fell, while AMD rose. Broadcom also went up. Nvidia has many deals with other AI companies, so it is hard to know how far the damage will spread. The stock has dropped roughly 30% over the past month. Watch for a permanent CEO announcement and any news about the investigation. Tonight's results from Cisco and Applied Materials will also show how strong AI demand is.

stories.title: Gold slides as traders price a December Fed hike
stories.why_happened: Traders now fully expect the Fed (the US central bank) to raise interest rates in December. This came after stronger US inflation (the rate prices rise) and tough talk from the Fed. The dollar also reached a 19-month high.
stories.why_matters: Higher interest rates and a stronger dollar make gold less attractive, because gold pays no interest.
stories.full: Gold had been hovering around $4,000. It dropped back below that level for the third time since late October. Tuesday's hotter US inflation report started the move. A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for buyers outside the US. Higher Treasury yields (the interest rate the US government pays on its bonds, which are loans to the government) make gold less appealing too. The drop spread across other metals. Silver fell 3.47% and copper slipped 1.8%. North American gold ETFs (funds that hold gold and trade like stocks) lost $512 million in October. That was the only region with money leaving, according to the World Gold Council. People who hold dollars and short-term bonds gain when yields rise. Gold mining companies, which make up a big part of Canada's stock market, face a weaker gold price. Next up is Friday's producer price report (a measure of inflation at the wholesale level). One strategist thinks gold could fall toward $3,870, near its late-October low, if the report comes in above forecasts.

stories.title: Bitcoin falls to its lowest since August
stories.why_happened: News about Nvidia's CEO and a decision by MSCI (a company that builds stock indexes) to remove Strategy from its indexes pushed bitcoin below $72,000.
stories.why_matters: Bitcoin is moving like a risky tech stock, and money leaving bitcoin funds is adding pressure.
stories.full: Bitcoin has moved with tech stocks for most of this month. Selling started after Wednesday's market close and picked up through the morning. Strategy is the largest company holder of bitcoin. Its shares fell about 7% at the open after MSCI confirmed it would be removed from its indexes. US spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin and trade like stocks) saw $299.8 million leave on Wednesday. That was their fifth straight day of money leaving, with about $1.44 billion gone over those five days. Leverage (borrowed money used to make bigger bets) made the drop worse. One count put crypto liquidations (forced sales of positions that lost too much value) at $656 million. The Binance Fear & Greed Index (a score of how scared or greedy crypto traders are) stood at 24, which signals extreme fear. Traders who borrow to bet lose the most in a drop like this. Funds that lost their index spot or face money leaving lose their steady buyers. One analyst points to support (a price level where buyers often step in) near the 200-day average (the average price over the last 200 trading days) and a zone between $70,000 and $71,500. Watch ETF money flows and Friday's PPI report.

deals.value: About $115 billion enterprise value (the total price, including debt), all in stock
deals.why: It combines Marvell's electrical technology with Lumentum's optical (light-based) expertise for AI data centers.
deals.full: Lumentum holders get 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own. They would own about 33% of the combined company. At announcement, that implied roughly $1,132 per Lumentum share. Marvell expects more than $1 billion a year in cost synergies (savings from combining the two companies) and says the deal will add to earnings (make earnings per share higher) in year one. Marvell fell almost 13% and Lumentum fell 18% on the news. The deal is more than ten times Marvell's previous largest deal. The expected savings only partly support the price. The deal shows how big companies are merging to build AI data center gear.

deals.why: Shield buys the maker of counter-drone radar (radar that spots and tracks hostile drones), and is raising $2.5 billion to pay for it.
deals.full: The price is $4.8 billion at closing, plus up to $500 million more if performance targets are met. Funding comes from $1 billion of conventional equity (regular shares sold to investors), $1 billion of structured equity (a custom mix of share-like funding), and $500 million of debt (borrowed money). The equity includes a $1 billion Series H (a type of private share sale) at a $28.8 billion valuation (the total value placed on the company). This shows that private defence-tech firms can make large purchases without first going public through an IPO (initial public offering, when a company first sells shares on a stock market).

deals.value: $2 billion underwritten share offering (a sale of new shares, with banks guaranteeing the sale)
deals.why: KDP shares fell 5% after it launched the sale.
deals.full: The offering is a straight sale of new shares. No valuation or details on how the money will be used were found. No major Canadian deals were found in the searches.

results.why: Revenue beat expectations, but shares still fell 19% because the 2026 revenue range came in slightly below estimates.

calendar.why: They show how strong demand is for AI networking and chip-making equipment.
Their comments can hint at where interest rates are heading.

intern.takeaway: When one company is at the center of a trend, news about its leaders can move the whole group, even when the broader market is fine.
intern.takeaway_accounting: A CEO change and an investigation can affect how investors value a company, so read the risks in the filings.
intern.takeaway_consulting: Key-person risk is real: when a leader leaves with no clear successor, clients and investors start to doubt the plan.

Using borrowed money to make a bigger bet, which can grow gains but also makes losses larger.

intern.calendar_note: Two items are coming up: tonight's Cisco and Applied Materials earnings, and Fed speeches later this week.
